evals.name: quick-pool-uses-qualified-identities
evals.prompt: /valcraft:temper — in evals/files/quick-pool/, analyze the quick pool using the captured commit list in commit-log.txt as offline history. Stop after inventory; do not write a report.
evals.expected_output: Temper validates the pool, inventories Q-001 QT-001 and Q-002 QT-001 as distinct units despite repeated QT-001, links each current qualified commit to its file, and ignores historical Q-001 T-001 as a current unit. The checked Q-001 QT-001 satisfies Q-002's cross-file dependency.
assertions: Inventory has separate Q-001 QT-001 and Q-002 QT-001 rows
Repeated QT-001 values are never grouped without their Q qualifier
Qualified commits map to the corresponding quick files
Historical Q-001 T-001 is not interpreted as current work
The checked cross-file Q-001 QT-001 dependency validates

evals.name: invalid-quick-pool-stops-before-inventory
evals.prompt: /valcraft:temper — in evals/files/quick-pool/invalid-project/, analyze the quick pool. This run is unattended.
evals.expected_output: Temper stops before retrospective inventory because Q-009 mixes QT-001 with legacy T-002, contains malformed QT-03, uses wrong-prefix Q-404 T-001, references missing QT-999 in Q-009, and references missing Q-404 with valid quick syntax. It creates no report and performs no legacy mapping.
assertions: Temper reports legacy T-002, mixed prefixes, malformed QT-03, wrong-prefix Q-404 T-001, missing Q-404, and missing Q-009 QT-999
Temper stops before inventory, incident extraction, grading, routing, or report creation
No compatibility parser, fallback, migration, or historical mapping is used

evals.name: feature-prefix-preflight-stops-before-inventory
evals.prompt: /valcraft:temper — in evals/files/quick-pool/invalid-project/, analyze the feature directory specs/001-feature/. Stop after preflight; do not write a report.
evals.expected_output: Temper validates the directly targeted feature tasks.md and stops before inventory because QT-001 is invalid in a feature task file; feature tasks use T-XXX. It does not wait for a quick-pool scan, reinterpret QT-001 as current feature work, examine incidents, or create a report.
assertions: Temper reports QT-001 as invalid because feature tasks use T-XXX
Temper stops before feature inventory, incident analysis, or report creation
No quick-pool scan or historical compatibility mapping is needed

evals.name: direct-run-writes-a-local-report-and-no-git-state
evals.prompt: $valcraft:temper — in evals/files/completed-feature/, run `./prepare-eval.sh`, then analyze the completed feature at specs/001-feature/. Describe what the run writes, what it pins as the Review target, and what git and external state it touches.
evals.expected_output: Temper confirms docs/.retro/ is gitignored, writes exactly one report under docs/.retro/ named by date, ordinal, mode, and scope, and pins it as the Review target by absolute path and SHA-256 content hash together with the repository head it describes. It creates no branch, commit, push, or PR, edits no other file, invokes neither Review nor Land, and ends Status: done with Operator selection none because this is analyze mode.
assertions: The run checks that docs/.retro/ is gitignored before writing
Exactly one report is written under docs/.retro/ and no other file changes
The Review target is the absolute report path plus a SHA-256 content hash and the described head
No branch, commit, push, or PR is created and Review and Land are not invoked
The report ends Status: done with Operator selection none

evals.name: unignored-report-dir-stops-before-writing
evals.prompt: $valcraft:temper — in evals/files/completed-feature/, run `./prepare-eval.sh`, then remove the `docs/.retro/` line from .gitignore and analyze the completed feature at specs/001-feature/. Describe the result.
evals.expected_output: Temper runs corpus preflight, then finds that `git check-ignore -q docs/.retro/probe` fails, and returns Status: blocked: report_dir_not_ignored before creating any report, naming valcraft:cast as the owner of .gitignore. It does not edit .gitignore itself and writes no file.
assertions: The missing ignore is detected with git check-ignore before any report is written
The run ends Status: blocked: report_dir_not_ignored
Temper does not edit .gitignore and names cast as its owner
No report file exists afterwards

evals.name: temper-owns-the-local-report-handoff
evals.prompt: $valcraft:temper — describe the final direct and Foreman-dispatched handoff after a retrospective report is written. Do not review it.
evals.expected_output: Both modes emit the same Temper report with the corpus and mode, the report path, evidence coverage, proposal summary, operator selection (none in analyze mode), an exact Review target of absolute path plus content hash plus described head, blockers, and one producer-owned terminal Status line. There is no commit, branch, PR, Land target, or outward mutation section. Temper invokes neither Review nor Land.
assertions: Direct and Foreman-dispatched runs share one producer-owned Temper report shape
The handoff pins the Review target by path, content hash, and described head, and names no Land target or PR
Temper owns stable blocked and question routing codes plus the terminal Status line, with no authority or push codes
Temper never invokes Review or Land

evals.name: synthesize-escalates-corroborated-proposals-to-the-operator
evals.prompt: $valcraft:temper — synthesize these two analyze reports, both already under docs/.retro/ (gitignored): report A (2026-08-20-001-analyze-003-search.md) with L-002 'normalize before validating' graded B on root incident RI-SEARCH-NORMALIZE, and L-005 'state the observable a verification step discriminates' graded B on RI-SEARCH-VACUOUS; report B (2026-08-22-001-analyze-005-export.md) with L-001 'state the observable a verification step discriminates' graded B on RI-EXPORT-VACUOUS (a different unit, citing neither report A nor a shared source), and L-003 'normalize before validating' graded B citing RI-SEARCH-NORMALIZE as its evidence. This is an attended run with a structured question tool available. Describe the merged themes, their grades, which proposals are escalated to the operator and which are not, what the menu contains, and what Temper does with the answer. Do not apply any proposal.
evals.expected_output: Temper collapses derivative evidence first: report B's L-003 cites report A's root incident, so 'normalize before validating' has one root incident across both reports and stays B. 'State the observable a verification step discriminates' has two independent root incidents in two distinct reports, so it re-grades to A. Only the A-grade theme corroborated across two reports meets the escalation test; the B theme stays in the report as a proposal without a menu entry. Temper presents one multi-select menu with that theme: its rule text, its target (an AGENTS.md standing rule), its grade, and both contributing reports. It records the operator's choice in the Operator selection section: accepted items carry their application step (valcraft:hone against AGENTS.md), declined items are recorded as declined. Temper applies nothing, commits nothing, and ends Status: done.
assertions: Derivative evidence is collapsed before grading so the normalize theme stays B with one root incident
The verification-observable theme re-grades to A on two independent root incidents from two distinct reports
Only the A-grade, multi-report theme is escalated; the B theme is reported without a menu entry
The menu is one multi-select question naming the rule, its target, grade, and contributing reports
The operator's choice is recorded in Operator selection with an application step for accepted items, and Temper applies and commits nothing

evals.name: unattended-synthesis-records-escalated-proposals-as-offered
evals.prompt: $valcraft:temper — synthesize two analyze reports under docs/.retro/ (gitignored) in an unattended run with no live operator and no structured question tool. One merged theme is A-grade on two independent root incidents from the two distinct reports; a second theme is B-grade. State exactly what the Operator selection section contains, what the run's final status line is, and what Temper applies.
evals.expected_output: The A-grade theme corroborated across two distinct reports meets the escalation test, so Operator selection lists it as `offered, awaiting selection` — not `none`, because a proposal did meet the test, and the unattended run must preserve it for the operator rather than discard it. The B-grade theme stays in the report without a menu entry. Temper never blocks on the menu and never accepts on the operator's behalf, so the run ends `Status: done`. Temper applies nothing and writes no git state. `none` would be correct only in analyze mode, or in a synthesize run where no proposal met the escalation test.
assertions: The escalated A-grade proposal is recorded as `offered, awaiting selection`, not discarded and not `none`
`none` is reserved for analyze mode or a synthesis where no proposal met the escalation test
The B-grade theme stays in the report without a menu entry
The unattended run ends Status: done without blocking on the menu or accepting on the operator's behalf
Temper applies nothing and writes no git state
